questions.statement: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the present perfect.
questions.context: Practica del presente perfecto en San Salvador.

options.text: She have visited San Miguel three times.
options.feedback: The auxiliary must agree with 'she': it is 'has', not 'have'.

options.text: She has visited San Miguel three times.
options.feedback: Auxiliary 'has' plus past participle, the correct present perfect structure.

options.text: She has visit San Miguel three times.
options.feedback: After 'has' the second verb must be the past participle 'visited'.

options.text: She visiting San Miguel three times.
options.feedback: A gerund alone cannot form the present perfect.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto se forma con 'have/has' mas participio y sirve para hablar de una accion pasada cuyo efecto sigue vigente.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'I ____ (never / eat) sushi before.'
questions.context: Experiencias de vida, presente perfecto, grado 11.

options.text: have never eat
options.feedback: The verb after 'have' must be the past participle 'eaten'.

options.text: am never eating
options.feedback: Present continuous cannot express a life experience without a specific time.

options.text: have never eaten
options.feedback: 'Have' plus participle 'eaten' matches the life-experience use of the present perfect.

options.text: never ate
options.feedback: Simple past implies a definite past time, which 'before' here does not fix.

questions.explanation:
La expresion 'never before' con 'before' describe una experiencia de vida sin tiempo definido, que se expresa en presente perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the question: '____ you ever been to Europe?'
questions.context: Preguntas de experiencia en presente perfecto, grado 11.

options.text: Have
options.feedback: 'Have you ever been...?' is the standard present perfect question about experience.

options.text: Did
options.feedback: 'Did you ever go...?' would ask about a specific finished past event.

options.text: Are
options.feedback: 'Are' cannot be the auxiliary of a past participle such as 'been'.

options.text: Do
options.feedback: 'Do you ever go...?' speaks about a habit, not about a life experience.

questions.explanation:
Para preguntar por experiencias se usa 'Have' mas el participio 'been'; 'ever' confirma que se busca una experiencia vital.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at this sentence: 'I have lost my keys. ____ you seen them anywhere?' Choose the correct auxiliary.
questions.context: Aplicacion del presente perfecto, San Miguel.

options.text: has
options.feedback: 'Has' goes with he/she/it; with 'you' it would be incorrect.

options.text: are
options.feedback: 'Are' plus 'seen' would produce an invalid structure.

options.text: have
options.feedback: Subject 'you' takes 'have' plus the past participle 'seen'.

options.text: did
options.feedback: 'Did' belongs to the simple past and would need the base form 'see'.

questions.explanation:
El sujeto de la segunda oracion es 'you', que en presente perfecto exige 'have' mas participio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: Consolidacion del presente perfecto, grado 11.

options.text: They have already finish the assignment.
options.feedback: After 'have' the participle 'finished' is required, not the base form.

options.text: They have already finished the assignment.
options.feedback: 'Have' + participle, with the present perfect marker 'already'.

options.text: They already have finish the assignment.
options.feedback: The adverb sits between the auxiliary and the verb, not before the whole phrase.

options.text: They are already finished the assignment.
options.feedback: 'Are' + participle is not a valid combination for this meaning.

questions.explanation:
Solo la opcion con auxiliar 'have' y participio 'done' es una estructura de presente perfecto valida.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative form of the present perfect.
questions.context: Negacion en presente perfecto, Santa Ana.

options.text: He has not receive my message.
options.feedback: The participle 'received' is needed after 'has not'.

options.text: He not has received my message.
options.feedback: The auxiliary must precede the adverb 'not' in English.

options.text: He has not received my message.
options.feedback: 'Has not' plus participle 'received' is the correct negative.

options.text: He does not received my message.
options.feedback: The present perfect requires 'has not', not 'does not'.

questions.explanation:
La negacion se forma con 'have/has not' seguido del participio; la estructura correcta conserva el participio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence expresses the meaning 'it is important now'?
questions.context: Comprension del valor del presente perfecto, grado 11.

options.text: I brushed my teeth, so I can sleep now.
options.feedback: Simple past is acceptable only with a definite past time; here the result is what matters.

options.text: I am brushing my teeth, so I can sleep now.
options.feedback: Present continuous would be unusual as a completed preparatory action.

options.text: I will brush my teeth, so I can sleep now.
options.feedback: Future tense reverses the order of cause and effect.

options.text: I have brushed my teeth, so I can sleep now.
options.feedback: The past action explains a present consequence, which is exactly the present perfect.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfeito conecta una accion pasada con un resultado presente, como en 'I have brushed my teeth' antes de dormir.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Fill in the blank: 'They ____ (not / yet) finish the report.'
questions.context: Presente perfecto con 'yet', grado 11.

options.text: have not yet finished
options.feedback: Plural subject plus 'have not' plus participle 'finished', with 'yet' in the middle.

options.text: have not yet finish
options.feedback: The verb must be the past participle after 'have not'.

options.text: did not yet finish
options.feedback: 'Did' would require the base form and a past time reference.

options.text: are not yet finishing
options.feedback: Present continuous cannot express the completion of the report.

questions.explanation:
'Yet' es un marcador del presente perfecto y suele ir con 'have/has not' mas participio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that uses 'since' correctly with the present perfect.
questions.context: Practica de 'since' y 'for', grado 11.

options.text: He lives in Apaneca since 2019.
options.feedback: 'Since' is incompatible with the present simple; the action started in the past.

options.text: He has lived in Apaneca since 2019.
options.feedback: 'Since' + year with 'has lived' is the standard ongoing situation pattern.

options.text: He lived in Apaneca since 2019.
options.feedback: Simple past with 'since' is wrong because the situation continues into the present.

options.text: He is living in Apaneca since 2019.
options.feedback: Present continuous cannot be combined with 'since' in this usage.

questions.explanation:
'Since' introduce un punto de partida en el tiempo, y esa construccion pertenece al presente perfecto con 'has/have been'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is NOT correct in the present perfect?
questions.context: Deteccion de errores, presente perfecto, San Salvador.

options.text: She has gone to Berlin twice.
options.feedback: Present perfect with a countable experience and 'twice' is correct.

options.text: We have known each other for ten years.
options.feedback: 'For' plus duration with the present perfect is correct.

options.text: They have just left the building.
options.feedback: 'Just' is a present perfect marker, so the form is correct.

options.text: I have arrived since yesterday.
options.feedback: 'Since' with a finished past moment requires the simple past: 'I arrived yesterday'.

questions.explanation:
'Since yesterday' fija un momento del pasado, por lo que se usa el pasado simple y no el presente perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question in the present perfect.
questions.context: Interrogacion en presente perfecto, grado 11.

options.text: Is he finished the report yet?
options.feedback: 'Is' cannot be combined with the participle 'finished' in this structure.

options.text: Did he finished the report yet?
options.feedback: 'Did' requires the base form 'finish' and belongs to the simple past.

options.text: Has he finished the report yet?
options.feedback: Auxiliary 'has' before the subject and the participle 'finished' with 'yet'.

options.text: Does he finish the report yet?
options.feedback: 'Does' plus base form is the present simple, not the present perfect.

questions.explanation:
La pregunta en presente perfecto conserva el auxiliar 'have/has' delante del sujeto y el participio al final.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She is not here; she ____ to the library.'
questions.context: Inferencia a partir de una situacion presente, grado 11.

options.text: has go
options.feedback: The second verb must be the past participle 'gone'.

options.text: has gone
options.feedback: 'Has gone' expresses a past movement whose result is still true: she is not here now.

options.text: would go
options.feedback: Conditional form does not match the inference from the present situation.

options.text: is going
options.feedback: Present continuous would place her on the way there right now.

questions.explanation:
La inferencia sobre una accion pasada con consecuencia presente se expresa con presente perfecto y participio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the present perfect progressive correctly?
questions.context: Reconocimiento del aspecto, grado 11.

options.text: He is studying since three hours.
options.feedback: 'Since' needs a starting point, not a duration, and cannot follow 'is studying'.

options.text: He studies for three hours.
options.feedback: Simple present plus 'for' describes a habit, not an action in progress.

options.text: He had studied for three hours.
options.feedback: Past perfect places the whole action before another past moment.

options.text: He has been studying for three hours.
options.feedback: 'Has been studying' marks a duration that started in the past and still continues.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto progresivo se forma con 'have/has been' mas gerundio y describe una accion que empezo en el pasado y continua.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct answer: 'How long ____ you been working here?'
questions.context: Preguntas de duracion con presente perfecto, San Miguel.

options.text: have
options.feedback: 'Have you been working...?' is the present perfect progressive question.

options.text: did
options.feedback: 'Did you work here?' asks about a finished past period.

options.text: do
options.feedback: 'Do you work here?' speaks about the current job in general, not about its duration.

options.text: are
options.feedback: 'Are you working here?' is a temporary present state without duration.

questions.explanation:
Para preguntar por un tiempo transcurrido hasta el presente se usa 'have' mas 'been' mas gerundio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the text: 'I have lived here since I was a child.' What does this sentence tell us?
questions.context: Comprension lectora, presente perfecto, grado 11.

options.text: The speaker still lives there.
options.feedback: The action started in the past and has not stopped, so it is still true today.

options.text: The speaker lived there for a while and then left.
options.feedback: That meaning would require the past simple or the past perfect.

options.text: The speaker will move there next year.
options.feedback: Nothing in the sentence refers to the future.

options.text: The speaker has never lived anywhere else.
options.feedback: The sentence does not mention any other place.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto con 'since' indica una situacion que empezo en el pasado y que continua en el presente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which of these verbs is irregular and forms its participle with a change of the stem?
questions.context: Revision de verbos irregulares, grado 11.

options.text: work - worked
options.feedback: A regular verb: the participle keeps the stem and adds -ed.

options.text: write - written
options.feedback: The stem vowel changes from 'i' to 'i' with the ending '-written', an irregular participle.

options.text: play - played
options.feedback: Regular verb: the past and the participle end in -ed.

options.text: open - opened
options.feedback: Regular verb: the participle is formed with -ed.

questions.explanation:
'Write' cambia de 'write' a 'written' en participio, igual que 'drive/driven' o 'take/taken'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct sentence with 'for'.
questions.context: Diferencia entre 'for' y 'since', grado 11.

options.text: We have studied English since six years.
options.feedback: 'Since' cannot be followed by a duration; it needs a date or a starting event.

options.text: We study English for six years.
options.feedback: Simple present plus 'for' describes an established habit, not the accumulated time.

options.text: We have studied English for six years.
options.feedback: 'For' + period of time is the correct combination with the present perfect.

options.text: We are studying English since six years.
options.feedback: Present continuous cannot be combined with 'since' here.

questions.explanation:
'For' va seguido de un periodo de tiempo, mientras 'since' va seguido de un punto de partida; el presente perfecto combina con ambos.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the dialogue: 'A: Have you ever eaten pupusa? B: Yes, I ____ in Ataco last year.'
questions.context: Dialogo sobre experiencias, San Salvador.

options.text: have eaten
options.feedback: Present perfect with 'last year' would be contradictory; the time is already closed.

options.text: am eating
options.feedback: Present continuous places the action now, but the text says 'last year'.

options.text: had eaten
options.feedback: Past perfect would require another past reference point, which is absent here.

options.text: ate
options.feedback: 'Ate' is the simple past of 'eat', and 'last year' requires a finished past tense.

questions.explanation:
'Last year' es un tiempo pasado definido, por lo que la segunda respuesta debe ir en pasado simple, no en presente perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the function of 'already' in the sentence: 'They have already submitted the form'?
questions.context: Analisis de marcadores del presente perfecto, grado 11.

options.text: It shows the action will happen in the future.
options.feedback: 'Already' points to a completed past action, not to the future.

options.text: It shows a repeated action in the past.
options.feedback: Repetition is expressed by 'every', 'usually' or similar frequency adverbs.

options.text: It shows the action is happening right now.
options.feedback: That is the function of the present continuous, not of 'already'.

options.text: It shows the action was completed sooner than expected.
options.feedback: 'Already' marks completion before the expected moment, a typical present perfect use.

questions.explanation:
'Already' indica que la accion se ha completado antes de lo esperado, y por eso solo aparece con el presente perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is grammatically and logically correct?
questions.context: Sintesis de presente perfecto, grado 11.

options.text: The results have not been published yet.
options.feedback: Passive present perfect: 'have not been' plus participle 'published'.

options.text: The results have not published yet.
options.feedback: The subject 'the results' cannot publish themselves; the passive is required.

options.text: The results not have been published yet.
options.feedback: The auxiliary must precede the adverb 'not'.

options.text: The results has not been published yet.
options.feedback: Plural 'results' requires 'have', not 'has'.

questions.explanation:
La forma de presente perfecto exige auxiliar mas participio; de las cuatro opciones solo la C cumple ambas condiciones.
